label: D1 candidate drops with consecutive unrewarded trials (reward-drought counter)
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (1 + (prev_state == S1)) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) * (tv("reward", -4) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == -9) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * np.abs(belief_lo) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.abs(belief_lo)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 26 is timing-dominated (D1 ~+0.8 falling late in the episode, GO ~-0.99, D2 ~+0.98; timing R^2 0.96). Beyond timing, nearly all variance is at D1 and tracks the run of unrewarded trials: an unrewarded previous trial lowers D1 (more after reaching S1 than S2), and each additional consecutive unrewarded trial (2, 3, 4 back) lowers it further (fitted -0.39, -0.27, -0.18), saturating near -0.8 after long droughts; when earlier history is outside the window a partial penalty applies. Reaching S2 on the last trial raises D1 (+0.13). Ideal-observer certainty |belief_lo| adds only a small amount (slightly higher when rewarded and certain). GO and D2 are near-constant (saturated); belief, current choice/state and the hidden good state matter little. Uses observed quantities only, no model outputs or future variables. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.557 vs all-cue ceiling 0.62 and all-observed 0.53; the earlier policy-based explanation is not needed, little is lost. Residual misses: partial recovery after a single reward following a long drought, and windows whose drought began before the window.

issues: The consecutive-drought structure holds up. Replacing the chained interaction terms with separate additive reward==0 flags for trials 1-4 back drops test R^2 to 0.478. A state-specific additive version (unrewarded at S1 vs at S2, 1-3 back) drops it to 0.438. So it really is a consecutive-run counter, as claimed.

The S1-vs-S2 asymmetry is real. The residual table shows D1 after a1 S1 u at -0.47 and after a2 S1 u at -0.375, against a1 S2 u at -0.13 and a2 S2 u at -0.06, and D1 after reaching S2 sits at about +0.13 to +0.18.

The belief terms add only about 0.017 (the six non-belief terms score 0.539 on test, all eight score 0.557), which matches 'adds only a little'. Other observed-belief variants (belief against the previous choice, signed belief_lo, belief_lo split by state) all land between 0.541 and 0.559, so no better observed-only signal was missed.

The largest remaining misses are systematic: the first D1 of a window is already near -0.8 while the prediction is about +0.5 to +0.6, because the drought began before the window. The single -9 term (weight -0.13) covers this only weakly. Within-window variables and belief cannot fix it, and the explanation acknowledges it.

Partial recovery after a single reward that follows a drought (actual about 0.2-0.55 vs predicted about 1.0) is under-modelled. Adding terms for 'rewarded after unrewarded' changes test R^2 only from 0.539 to 0.554, so this is a small, acknowledged gap.
There is a modest residual bias at D1 after a2 S2 u (+0.12 under-predicted). A dedicated last_is('a2 S2 u') term does not improve test R^2 (0.551), so it is not a large error class.

The claim that dropping value/policy costs little is not tested directly here. Support for it is the score of 0.557 against the all-cue ceiling of 0.62 (which includes policy) and the all-observed reference of 0.53, which is reasonable.
